transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because since they changed my hours at the warehouse and started using this new inventory system, I just… I feel like I’m falling apart. I’ve been missing shifts, missing things at church, snapping at my family. Some mornings I put my work boots on and just sit there wondering if I can even face going in.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like church or other activities?

I’m not really sure I’d put it that way. I mean, I haven’t been making it to church like I used to, but I don’t know if it’s because I don’t care about it anymore. It’s more like I just… don’t get there.
Have you noticed that things you used to look forward to, like church or spending time with family, don’t bring you any joy or satisfaction anymore?
I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed it that clearly. I still care about church and my family. It’s just been harder to get myself there or be fully present, I guess.
Do you find yourself feeling down or low most days, even when there’s no clear reason for it?

I don’t know if it’s most days, exactly. I wouldn’t say it comes out of nowhere either. When I feel low, it usually feels tied to all this work stuff and how I’m not keeping up. But I haven’t really been tracking it day by day.
Can you describe how long you’ve been feeling this way, and whether there have been days where you felt better or it's been pretty consistent?

It’s been about five months now, I’d say. It really started when they changed the warehouse schedule and brought in that new inventory system. Since then it’s been pretty steady, though I guess some days are a little better than others.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or like you're not good enough, even when things aren't necessarily your fault?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I do get frustrated with myself when I can’t keep up like I used to, but I don’t know if I’d call it guilt. It’s more just feeling like I should be doing better.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or lacking in energy most days, even when you haven’t done anything particularly strenuous?

I’m not really sure. I mean, at my age and with the kind of work I do, I expect to be tired sometimes. I haven’t noticed it being most days when I haven’t done much, though. It’s hard for me to separate.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or thinking clearly, especially when it comes to your work or daily tasks?

I don’t know that I’d say trouble thinking clearly. At work, I might get a little mixed up sometimes with all the changes, but I can usually figure it out. I haven’t really noticed it happening in my daily stuff much.
Can you describe if there have been times when you’ve felt down or hopeless even when things at work were going okay, or does your low mood seem to only happen because of the stress at work?

It really seems tied to the work stress. Since they changed my warehouse hours and brought in that new inventory system, I’ve felt like I’m falling apart. I’ve missed shifts, missed things at church, and I’ve been snapping at my family. Some mornings I’m sitting there with my work boots on, and I just don’t know if I can face going in.
Have you ever felt down or hopeless when things at work weren’t particularly stressful, or does your low mood only happen when work is bothering you?

It’s really when work is bothering me. I didn’t come in because I was just feeling hopeless out of nowhere. It started after they changed my warehouse hours and put in that new inventory system. Since then I feel like I’m falling apart—missing shifts, missing things at church, snapping at my family. Some mornings I’m sitting there in my work boots wondering if I can even face going in.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, even when things at work weren’t particularly stressful?

No, not really apart from this work situation. I came in because since they changed my hours at the warehouse and brought in that new inventory system, I feel like I’m falling apart. I’m missing shifts, missing church commitments, snapping at my family… and some mornings I just sit there in my work boots wondering if I can even face going in.
